weather_reasons: NWS hourly forecast includes thunderstorm potential
Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 282100
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
200 PM MST Fri Aug 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Extreme Heat Warnings remain in effect through Saturday with 
  areas of Major to Extreme Heat Risk, despite temperatures slowly
  decreasing.

- Today will bring low end chances for showers and isolated 
  thunderstorms, with a low probability for strong to severe 
  outflow winds and blowing dust focused in Southeast California.

- An approaching low pressure system will bring much better 
  chances for rain, including a chance of strong to severe storms 
  across Southern Arizona mainly on Sunday and Monday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Analysis of midlevel WV imagery reveals that the flow aloft is in
the process of shifting from southeasterly to 
southerly/southwesterly as Pacific troughing impinges on the 
forecast area from the northwest. The upstream troughing has begun
to impact the subtropical ridge more noticeably, displacing the 
high eastward with some signs of weakening early this afternoon 
compared to previous days. This will become much more apparent 
tonight into Saturday, as ensembles continue to be in excellent 
agreement that H5 heights will drop from the current 594-597 dam 
closer to 591-594 dam tomorrow. Midlevel moisture transport from 
over Sonora is noted in the water vapor imagery as well and has 
become apparent in the 12Z PSR sounding with PWAT analyzed at 
1.57", up from 1.26" yesterday. Low level moisture, however, 
remains generally unsupportive (marginally supportive at best) for
the formation/maintenance of lower desert thunderstorms, with 
1000-700 mb mean mixing ratios still below 10 g/kg, but hovering 
close to 9 g/kg across much of the area.

Through the rest of today, moisture looks to remain fairly 
constant, with midlevel subsidence still evident in area GFS bufr 
soundings, which makes sense given anticyclonic flow aloft. 
However, with this amount of moisture, only one outflow boundary 
passing through an area may be enough to moisten the low levels 
sufficiently to support deep moist convection if followed by 
another lifting mechanism (second outflow boundary). Inverted-V 
soundings and DCAPEs around 1000-1500+ J/kg areawide will mean 
that distant thunderstorms over AZ high terrain and portions of 
Southeast AZ are likely to form long- lived outflows, pushing into
South-Central AZ lower deserts during the evening. The most 
likely outcome for the Greater Phoenix Area this evening would be 
another round of isolated-scattered elevated showers and storms 
forming later in the evening or overnight from earlier outflows or
distant gravity waves. As steering flow transitions out of the 
southwest, particularly across the western CWA, there will be 
better chances for decaying thunderstorms to move off the Baja 
Spine into Imperial County mid to late this afternoon. HREF 
probabilities indicate a potential for additional development of 
thunderstorms over the Southeast CA deserts and even 10-30% 
neighborhood probabilities of 58+ mph wind gusts near storms, but 
these storms will be feeding off a decaying source of instability 
as southwesterly flow rapidly dries the lower levels. A 10% 
neighborhood probability for severe gusts is also indicated over 
prominent terrain of Central/northeastern La Paz County late this 
afternoon into the evening. If this comes to fruition, expect 
areas of blowing dust to cause reductions in visibility that could
become hazardous to motorists/aviation users across portions of 
Southeast CA and Southwest AZ (mainly La Paz County).

What occurs Saturday afternoon/evening is still quite uncertain 
as it will be more of a conditional type environment for storm 
development. Moisture is expected to have increased enough to 
bring MUCAPEs up to around 1000 J/kg into South-Central Arizona, 
but not enough to erase all of the CIN. The question is where 
exactly will showers and storms develop Saturday afternoon and if 
a large enough cluster can develop to force a strong or multiple 
outflows into the lower deserts. It is looking more encouraging 
for storm potential as the amount of CIN does not look too high 
and any decent outflow should overcome it. We will also start to 
see some upper level support from the incoming trough. Latest HREF
consensus is for storms to eventually congeal over Central Pima 
County then trend northwards over the Tabletop Wilderness and 
southern Pinal County, sending outflows northward towards the 
Greater Phoenix Area during the early evening, with isolated- 
scattered development of elevated showers/storms behind those 
outflows. Saturday should also be the last of the extreme heat 
with forecast highs dropping to 107-111 degrees before a much more
noticeable cool down begins Sunday.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/... 
Sunday and/or Monday are still looking quite interesting for
thunderstorm potential with the environment potentially supporting
some severe storms. Some ingredients for strong to severe storms 
are expected to be present, like upper level support and 
sufficient instability, but wind shear will be somewhat lacking. 
Moisture is forecast to improve enough to support a nearly 
uncapped environment across south-central Arizona Sunday and 
potentially again Monday afternoon with MUCAPEs as high as
1500-1800 J/kg. Both days have the potential to bring scattered 
to numerous showers and thunderstorms across south-central and 
eastern Arizona. Strong to localized severe wind gusts, blowing 
dust, heavy rainfall, and flooding all look possible, but as 
stated above the threat may be localized due to the fairly weak 
shear which is oftentimes needed to sustain strong storms or
clusters of storms. We should have a better idea on how this 
strong to severe storm threat may evolve by Saturday/Saturday 
night. Guidance then suggests some drying will occur by Tuesday 
which should decrease rain chances substantially through the 
middle of next week. 

Temperatures will drop into or even just below normal early next
week, but highs are still forecast to top 100 degrees each day
across the lower deserts. Once the drier air moves into the region
by the middle of next week, we expect temperatures to quickly warm
to a few degrees above normal but with little chance of reaching
110 degrees again. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1735Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

A gusty southerly outflow with some lofted haze this evening will
be the primary aviation weather issue during the next 24 hours. 
In the meantime, winds will gradually shift out of the west by the
early to mid-afternoon hours with a period of southerly winds 
before the eventual westerly shift. Overall speeds through this 
afternoon are forecast to remain aob 10 kts. Thereafter, guidance 
continues to show a southerly outflow from convective activity in
southeast AZ propagating into the area, sometime between 03-06z, 
with some gusty winds potentially upwards of 25-30 kts as well as 
some reduced VIS due to lofted HZ/BLDU. After the outflow passage
later this evening, VCSH is possible during the overnight period,
mainly between 06-12z, with minimal operational impacts expected.
SCT to at times BKN mid/high cloud decks will be common through 
the period. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

Isolated TS activity, especially at KIPL, this afternoon will be 
the primary aviation weather issue during the next 24 hours. 
Winds will fluctuate between the southeast to west at KIPL and 
south to southwest at KBLH. Heading into this afternoon, TS 
activity over the Baja Spine may drift into the Imperial Valley,
affecting KIPL, however, there continues to be uncertainty in the
overall coverage and intensity of the TS activity and thus a
PROB30 remains in the latest TAF package. If a TS would to
materialize, gusty winds and reduced VIS due to HZ/BLDU will be
the main impacts. KBLH may see an outflow from the activity to
the southwest, but confidence remains too low for inclusion in 
the latest TAF package. FEW-SCT mid/high cloud decks will be 
common throughout the period, with occasional BKN decks with any 
convective activity. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Hot and relatively dry conditions will continue into this weekend,
but with slight chances for isolated showers and thunderstorms. 
Chances then increase considerably by Saturday night/Sunday, 
especially across Southern and Central Arizona. Afternoon minimum 
humidities will range between 17-25% Saturday and 15-30% areawide
Sunday following fair to good overnight recoveries. Winds will be
relatively light and follow diurnal tendencies through tonight 
before south to southwesterly winds increase this weekend, 
particularly across the western deserts, where afternoon gusts 
increase up to 20-30 mph. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST Saturday for AZZ530>555-559-
     560.

     Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST this evening for AZZ556-561-
     562.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT Saturday for CAZ562-565>567-
     569-570.

     Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT this evening for CAZ561-563-
     564-568.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock/Kuhlman
LONG TERM...Kuhlman
AVIATION...Lojero
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock/Kuhlman
